sam_sales: FYI acme POC can't see trace IDs in Azure Monitor exports. They only see request ids and timestamps, no W3C trace IDs. Customer says it's blocking verification for SRE team.

maya_eng: Are they hitting our hosted API or Dedicated?

sam_sales: Hosted API (api.redwood.ai). They claim they set `traceparent` and `x-request-id` on their side, but nothing shows up in the exported traces.

anika_reliability: Can you paste a minimal request example (headers + curl) and any runtime log lines?

sam_sales: Sure — here's the snippet they sent:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01" \
  -H "x-request-id: p123-req-456" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hello"}'
```

maya_eng: Thanks. Two quick suspects: (1) their frontend/proxy (nginx/ingress) might be stripping `traceparent`. (2) older versions of our SDK didn't forward W3C headers by default. Which SDK version are they on?

sam_sales: They said `redwood-js-sdk` v1.1.3 in their package.json.

anika_reliability: That's likely it — v1.1.3 has a forwarded-headers bug where `traceparent` can be dropped when the SDK builds the outgoing request. Workaround: set the header explicitly in the app before SDK call or configure proxy to preserve headers. We'll provide config.

nina_oncall: Pasting our runtime warn line they reported from their logs: 
```
2026-02-22T15:04:12.831Z WARN incoming-request missing traceparent header for request id=p123-req-456 origin=acmesvc
```

maya_eng: Ok. Workarounds: (A) Upgrade to `redwood-js-sdk` >= 1.2.1 (contains the header-forwarding fix). (B) If they can't upgrade, add this nginx snippet to force passthrough: 
```
# nginx.conf snippet to preserve W3C trace headers
proxy_set_header Traceparent $http_traceparent;
proxy_set_header tracestate $http_tracestate;
proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $http_x_request_id;
proxy_pass_request_headers on;
```

anika_reliability: Also for Azure Monitor Kusto query, here's a quick join to correlate logs and traces by trace id (replace table names as needed):
```
requests
| where timestamp > ago(1d)
| extend trace = tostring(parse_json(tostring(customDimensions.traceparent)))
| project timestamp, trace, operation_Id, name
| join kind=leftouter ( traces | project traceId, duration ) on $left.trace == $right.traceId
```

mike_support: Created support ticket POC-4821 and linked the ACME sales opportunity. Assigned to eng-trace-team. redwood-deploy-bot: deployed redwood-js-sdk@1.2.1 to canary yesterday. :rocket:

redwood-deploy-bot: Deployment url: https://deploys.redwood.ai/canary/2026-02-21-1723

nina_oncall: I'll repro locally with an nginx reverse proxy + SDK v1.1.3 to confirm. ETA ~4h. If I can reproduce I'll prepare a tiny patch we can give the customer as a hotfix script.

sam_sales: Great — I'll send the nginx snippet + KQL to the customer and ask them to try setting the header manually in the meantime. Also asked if they'd consider switching to Dedicated for the POC but they prefer not to change infra right now.

anika_reliability: One more note for the customer: if they use Azure App Gateway or Application Gateway v1, verify "preserve_client_ip" or header forwarding settings; gateways are notorious for header normalization.

sam_sales: Thanks everyone — will update the ticket after ACME tests the workaround. :thumbsup:
